title: Orchard and Compass
premise: In 1899, on the tidal straits of a Pacific coast trading post, Marguerite Lockridge has spent fifteen years as an indentured clerk to the Meridian Trading Company, hiding the pearl-diving knowledge inherited from her drowned mother and the promise she made to a boy from the rival island village: that she would return his family's compass when the war fever passed. When the season's first storm closes the only bridge and the government declares his people enemy aliens, the compass becomes evidence of treason — and Marguerite the only person who can carry it across the water. Smuggling it means betraying the company that owns her debt and the found family of clerks who have become her home. She chooses the promise, loses her indenture and nearly her life crossing the strait, and ends the century not free exactly, but self-owned for the first time, standing on the far shore with the compass returned and her mother's diving knife in her belt.
about_author: T. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers from Pacific coast trading posts before turning to fiction. They write about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous' — the indentured, the interpreters, and the children who kept both sides' secrets.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Opening in the Meridian Company counting house, where she audits debts with a precision that hides how much of her own life is owed. Establishes her found family of clerks, the weight of her indenture, and the compass hidden in a floorboard. Emotional beat: the ache of a life measured in entries not her own.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with a flashback to her mother's last dive. She recalls the promise made at fourteen to Emeric Sato, the boatbuilder's son: keep the compass, return it when it's safe. The village across the strait is now under surveillance. Emotional beat: grief surfacing like a body the tide refuses to surrender.

chapters.title: The Bridge Season
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, mostly Marguerite's POV. Storm warnings close the tidal bridge for winter; the company rushes last shipments. Mr. Calloway, the factor, announces new security regulations targeting the island village. Emotional beat: the claustrophobia of watching walls go up around people you love.

chapters.title: A Letter in Two Hands
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A smuggled letter from Emeric arrives via a fisherman: his father has been arrested, the family's boats seized, and he asks only for the compass — his grandfather's — before the confiscations reach his mother's house. Emotional beat: a promise made in peacetime arriving like a summons.

chapters.title: The Factor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. He suspects Marguerite's loyalties but values her too much to confront her; instead he offers to buy out the last year of her indenture if she informs on 'suspicious correspondence.' Emotional beat: the seduction of safety offered by someone who means it kindly and damns you anyway.

chapters.title: Salt and Iron
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She rehearses the crossing her mother taught her — tides, currents, the reef channel no patrol boat watches. The clerks' household notices her distraction; her closest friend, Ada, covers for her without asking why. Emotional beat: the loneliness of preparing a betrayal you haven't confessed.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Household
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Government agents inventory the company's records, hunting 'enemy assets.' Ada discovers the compass's hiding place while cleaning and says nothing, but now carries the same danger. Emotional beat: found family tested by the discovery that love means sharing risk unasked.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A clerk is arrested for a smaller kindness than hers; the household must decide whether to testify for him and mark themselves. Calloway pressures Marguerite again. Emotional beat: watching the cost of survival mount in other people's names.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours of Tide
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She calculates a window: a spring tide in four days when the reef channel runs deep enough for a small boat and fog will cover the crossing. She tells Ada everything. Emotional beat: the terror and relief of being known completely.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, interwoven with her mother's voice in memory. She visits the grave on the bluff, asks permission she already knows the answer to, and takes her mother's diving knife. Emotional beat: inheritance not as property but as obligation.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A clerk in the household, frightened for his own family, reports 'unusual activity' — not naming Marguerite, but close enough. Calloway begins quietly watching the counting house at night. Emotional beat: betrayal committed out of love, which is the cruelest kind.

chapters.title: Crossing at Slack Water
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The first crossing attempt fails — fog lifts early, a patrol gunboat forces her back into the reeds. She loses her boat but keeps the compass and knife. Emotional beat: failure that clarifies; she is committed now, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. He confronts Marguerite with what he knows — not enough to charge her, enough to own her. He offers again: inform, and the indenture dissolves. She refuses without explaining, and he cannot decide if it's loyalty or defiance. Emotional beat: two people who respect each other on a collision course.

chapters.title: The Household Decides
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Ada's POV anchoring. The clerks vote, in effect, by action: Ada forges a requisition for a company skiff, the old cook packs food, the arrested clerk's brother provides tide charts. Emotional beat: found family choosing her over their own safety, one small treason at a time.

chapters.title: Reef Channel
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The second crossing, at night, through the reef her mother named for her. Near-drowning; the knife and compass lashed to her body; the moment she almost turns back. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full, in cold water and terror.

chapters.title: The Far Shore
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. The internment zone at dawn: guarded, half-empty, families waiting for transport. Marguerite arrives soaked and half-frozen; Emeric barely recognizes the child he promised nothing to and everything. She returns the compass. Emotional beat: a promise kept in the wreckage of the world that made it.

chapters.title: What the Compass Points To
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. The compass is more than heirloom: inside the case is the deed to the family's boatyard, hidden there years ago, the only untainted proof of ownership that might survive the confiscations. Marguerite's delivery may save more than memory. Emotional beat: the discovery that faithfulness outlasts its own forgetting.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Split POV, Marguerite and Calloway, New Year's Eve. She is caught returning — not by soldiers but by Calloway, who waited on the dock. Bells ring in 1900. He must choose: report her or burn the evidence. Emotional beat: the climax held in a single handshake that is also a pardon and an accusation.

chapters.title: Terms of Release
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. He destroys the report and releases her from indenture — not as mercy, he insists, but because an employee who would cross open water for a promise is worth more free than owned. Marguerite knows it's a lie shaped like kindness and accepts it anyway. Emotional beat: freedom given grudgingly is still freedom.

chapters.title: Diving Lessons
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Spring: she teaches Emeric's younger sister the reef channels their grandmother worked, the knowledge her mother left her finally passed on. The boatyard reopens under the recovered deed. Emotional beat: inheritance completing its circle, from mother to daughter to stranger-become-family.

chapters.title: The Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Marguerite returns to the counting house one last time — not as a debtor but to settle the household's own small debts, the borrowed boots, the forged requisition, the silences. Calloway enters her final line: 'Paid in full.' Emotional beat: accounting as forgiveness; every entry balanced.

chapters.title: Orchard and Compass
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, final chapter. Years later, on the replanted hillside above the strait, she watches the bridge reopen and the first ferry cross. The compass hangs by her door, pointing not north but home. Emotional beat: the quiet triumph of a life self-owned, promised, and kept.
